issues.failure_explanation: The weighted residual R̄_Q applies different weight functions to different operator components. Writing R̄_Q = φ_θ¹ R_Q + Σ(φ_θ¹−φ_θ̄^i)∂_{x_ix_i}u + (φ_θ²−φ_θ¹)v(u) + (φ_θ¹−φ_θ³)f1_ω, the extra cross-weight mismatch terms do not vanish at the exact solution when weights differ. The proof bounds ||R̄_Q(u_ε,f_ε)|| as if it were P times the standard residual ||R_Q||, ignoring these terms entirely. Similarly, the boundary residual contains paired weights such as φ_θ⁶u_θ(0)−φ_θ⁷u_0, which at u_θ(0)=u_0 equals (φ_θ⁶−φ_θ⁷)u_0 ≠ 0 when φ_θ⁶≠φ_θ⁷, yet the proof claims ||R̄_Γ|| ≤ P||u_θ−u||_{H¹(Γ)} which would force this term to vanish as u_θ→u.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the weight parameters to be uniformly close to 1 (e.g. ||φ−1||_∞ ≤ ε for small ε) so that the cross-weight mismatch terms are O(ε·||u||) and can be absorbed into the constants, then redo the residual estimates including these terms. This yields a convergence rate with an additional O(ε) contribution but weakens the quantifier from "for any parameters" to "for parameters close to 1."
issues.overall_effect: The approximation theorems (thm:errorHeat, thm:errorWave, thm:errorHeatb, thm:errorWaveb) are not established. The claim that the weighted loss can be driven to C₃(W^{-1/d}L^{-1/d}+δ)² for arbitrary weight parameters is unsupported because the proofs ignore contributions from unequal weight functions on different operator and boundary components.
issues.title: Weighted residual estimates ignore cross-weight mismatch terms
issues.why_classification: The quantifier "for any parameters" is a central claim of all four theorems. Restricting weights to be near 1 changes this quantifier and excludes the advertised regime of arbitrary adversarial weight configurations. Alternatively, a construction choosing u_θ to solve the weighted PDE would require essentially new proof architecture. No repair preserves the full "for any parameters" scope at the stated rate.

issues.failure_explanation: The correct boundary integral from integrating by parts is ∫∂Ω u_θ(∇û·ν) since û=u_θ on ∂Ω and û=u_θ−ū. The proof writes ∫∂Ω u_θ(∇u_θ·ν), omitting the term −∫∂Ω u_θ(∇ū·ν). Moreover, the bound ∫∂Ω u_θ(∇u_θ·ν) ≤ (1/2)||u_θ||²_{H¹(∂Ω)} is false: H¹(∂Ω) contains only tangential derivatives of u_θ on ∂Ω, while ∇u_θ·ν is the normal derivative. For u_θ=0 on ∂Ω we have ||u_θ||²_{H¹(∂Ω)}=0 but ||∇u_θ·ν||²_{L²(∂Ω)}>0 in general (it equals ||∂u/∂ν||²_{L²(∂Ω)} at the exact solution). The correct Cauchy–Schwarz bound gives ∫∂Ω u_θ(∇û·ν) = O(√δ) instead of O(δ), degrading the final rate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the boundary integral to ∫∂Ω u_θ(∇û·ν) and bound it via Cauchy–Schwarz as ||u_θ||_{L²(∂Ω)}||∇û·ν||_{L²(∂Ω)} = O(√δ). Accept the degraded O(√δ) rate in the conclusion instead of O(δ).
issues.overall_effect: The state-error estimate ||u−u_θ||² ≤ Cδ claimed by thm:error_estHeat and thm:error_estWave degrades to ||u−u_θ||² ≤ C√δ. The qualitative convergence conclusion survives but at a strictly weaker rate than stated.
issues.title: Boundary term in energy estimate uses wrong function and wrong norm
issues.why_classification: The repair is local to the energy-estimate boundary bound and requires no new global proof architecture. The convergence rate weakens from O(δ) to O(√δ) but the qualitative guarantee (error→0 as δ→0) survives as a recognizably comparable result.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited controllability estimate bounds the minimal/constructed control for steering ũ from ũ(0)=u₀−ū(0) to ũ(T)=0 by C||ũ(0)||. However, f−f_θ̄ is a specific control achieving this steering determined by the given f and the neural network f_θ̄, not the minimal control. For the heat equation the control operator A: g ↦ ũ_g(0) has non-trivial kernel, so f−f_θ̄ can contain a kernel component making ||f−f_θ̄|| arbitrarily larger than the minimal control norm. The bound ||f−f_θ̄|| ≤ C||ũ(0)|| does not follow from the cited result and is false in general.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish ||f−f_θ̄|| ≤ C||ũ(0)|| for the specific control f−f_θ̄ (not merely the minimal control), or find an entirely different argument to bound ||f−f_θ̄|| in terms of δ. One possible route is to additionally assume f is the minimal control and prove that f−f_θ̄ has no component in ker(A), but this requires a new lemma not present in the source.
issues.overall_effect: The control-error conclusion ||f−f_θ̄||² ≤ Cδ of thm:error_estHeat and thm:error_estWave is unsupported. Without bounding ||f−f_θ̄||, the state-error bound ||u−u_θ||² ≤ Cδ also fails to close (since ||u−u_θ||² ≤ C(||f−f_θ̄||²+δ) from the energy estimates for ũ and û).
issues.title: Control error estimate misapplies controllability result to non-minimal control
issues.why_classification: The unjustified estimate is the sole mechanism connecting the hypothesis to the control-error conclusion. Closing the gap requires a fundamentally new argument (e.g. proving f−f_θ̄ is minimal for the difference system) or adding a new hypothesis on f. Without this, the main conclusion of both error-estimation theorems is unsupported, so no comparable version of the stated guarantee survives under the current proof architecture.
